A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Score as Action research work. Their complete 19-page documents, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original CIFAR-10 and Stable Diffusion fine-tuning experiments, value-network ablations, discretization tests, and generated samples in Table 1 and Figures 1–9.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds reward-curve comparisons against DRaFT and AlignProp in Appendix C.1, Figure 10.

M1.justification: The score-as-action formulation, Gaussian exploration, KL objective, value-network architecture, and continuous-time policy updates are unchanged. Algorithm 1 moves from Appendix C.1 to C.2 without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain CIFAR-10 short-step generation and Stable Diffusion text-to-image fine-tuning and discretization tests. The added baseline comparison introduces no new dataset, task, or input scenario.

E2.justification: The Stable Diffusion comparison expands from DDPO in Figure 9 to DDPO, DRaFT, and AlignProp in the new Figure 10. This substantially broadens comparator coverage to non-RL fine-tuning alternatives; the CIFAR-10 comparison against DxMI is retained.

E3.justification: The reported datasets, model settings, learning rates, batch size, and evaluation metrics are retained. Figure 10 uses the existing reward-mean-versus-epoch evaluation with 50 discretization steps, without reporting a distinct protocol or revision to existing settings.

E4.justification: The value-network ablations in Table 1/Figure 2, discretization tests in Figures 1 and 7, and qualitative samples are unchanged. Figure 10 adds comparator results without introducing a separate ablation, robustness test, or diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: v3 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained plots and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 10 adds DRaFT and AlignProp reward curves, ending near 1.73 and 1.71 at epoch 60, below CTRL's approximately 1.90. It redisplays the existing CTRL/DDPO trajectories; Table 1 and the results in Figures 1–9 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorem statements, Appendix A sampler derivations, and Appendix B proofs are unchanged. No new mathematical result or correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: continuous-time score-based control, diffusion-informed value networks, and scalable policy optimization theory. Added terminology clarifications do not change these claims.

C2.justification: The discretization-error explanation, robustness interpretation, and qualifications concerning value-function approximation and alternative evaluation methods retain their substance. The new generic Impact Statement adds no specific limitation or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly states that the DRaFT implementation was modified from AlignProp. Existing implementation information, including LoRA use, learning rates, hardware, batch size, and algorithm pseudocode, is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Clark et al. (2023) for DRaFT and Prabhudesai et al. (2023) for AlignProp, positioning them as non-RL fine-tuning comparators. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Limited edits clarify discretization errors, identify sample prediction as x-prediction, and refine experimental prose. v3 adds an Impact Statement and comparison subsection C.1, renumbers the pseudocode subsection, and updates the publication notice without broadly reorganizing the narrative.

P2.justification: v3 adds the four-method Figure 10 while retaining Figure 9. Other changes comprise minor Figure 1 cleanup, caption edits, and page reflow; Table 1 and the remaining original visual content are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix C.1 and Figure 10 improve the empirical context by adding relevant non-RL competitors missing from v2, with a small implementation disclosure and useful wording clarifications. The gain remains limited to the existing evaluation setting, with little baseline-specific implementation detail and no additional statistical uncertainty reporting.
